ambiguities.text: The EIP does not specify behavior when a transaction's actual execution uses less gas than its limit but the limit exceeds the cap.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume validation is based solely on the declared gasLimit field, not actual gas usage. A transaction with gasLimit > 16,777,216 is invalid even if execution would use less.

ambiguities.text: The phrase 'large contract deployments may require re-architecting' does not specify what architectural patterns should be used.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume developers must use CREATE2 factory patterns, proxy patterns, or split deployments across multiple transactions to stay within the cap.

ambiguities.text: The EIP states the cap applies independent of block gas limits 'which may exceed this value' but doesn't specify interaction semantics.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume a block can have total gas > 16,777,216 by including multiple transactions, each individually under the cap.

implicit_assumptions.description: All legitimate use cases can be accomplished within the 16,777,216 gas limit or restructured to fit.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Some existing contracts or deployment patterns may become impossible to execute, breaking backward compatibility.

implicit_assumptions.description: DoS attacks are primarily enabled by high individual transaction gas consumption rather than transaction volume.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Attackers could still execute DoS via high volume of cap-compliant transactions, making the mitigation less effective.

implicit_assumptions.description: dApps and tooling will update to enforce the new cap before activation.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Users may experience transaction failures if their wallets or tooling allow setting gas limits above the cap.
